transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (NebulaWorks Head of Platform), Priya (Eng Mgr), Samir (Security)

Summary:
High-level activation handshake and runbook orientation for NebulaWorks' pilot with Redwood. Covered roles/responsibilities, staging vs prod network connectors, basic SSO/KMS ask, and a plan for a small pilot benchmark. Several clarifications about dedicated vs hosted options and cost/latency trade-offs. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Roles and primary contacts
- Access and environment provisioning (staging account, API keys, VPC peering)
- Security/compliance notes (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot scope and success criteria (latency SLO, throughput targets)
- Observability and runbook walkthrough
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan: Jordan here, Head of Platform at NebulaWorks.
[00:08] Priya: Priya, engineering manager, focusing on integrations.
[00:12] Samir: Samir, security architect.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan Liu, solutions engineer, I'll run through the runbook and perf bits.
[00:20] Maya: Great, thanks. The aim today is the activation handshake — what we call the runbook orientation — walk through who does what and get the staging access items in motion. We have ~60 mins so we'll try to keep it tight.
[00:34] Jordan: Sounds good. We want to make sure the pilot doesn't surprise our infra team, so networking and KMS are biggest for us.
[00:40] Samir: Yea, and I'll add audit log retention / e-discovery questions. We have specific retention needs for at least 3 years.
[00:47] Ethan: Got it. I will flag places where Redwood exposes logs (console, API) and how to forward to Splunk or their SIEM. Quick note: sometimes the auto-transcription calls our product Redwood Dedicate instead of Dedicated, sorry the transcript is weird, but the product we reference is Redwood Dedicated or our hosted API depending on the plan.
[01:05] Priya: Quick Q — what's the recommended route for us? We're leaning private deployment because of PII, but maybe we start hosted and move?
[01:12] Maya: Good question. We often recommend a two-phased approach: pilot on Hosted API for speed, then lift to Dedicated or Private if you need VPC/air-gap. Pilot on hosted reduces setup time and we can measure latency/cost quickly. But if your compliance team insists on VPC from day one that's fine — it'll add network setup time.
[01:30] Jordan: Our compliance team prefers VPC but will accept an isolated staging to evaluate. We want a clean comparison though — so if we run hosted pilot, can we get the same model variants later on Dedicated?
[01:38] Ethan: Yes, that's one of Redwood's points: model pinning and consistent runtime across deployment modes. You can pin model versions and replicate the config later. There might be slight perf variances depending on hardware and quantization, but the API surface is consistent.
[01:52] Samir: On encryption, we use a customer-managed KMS in GCP. Does Redwood support bringing your own KMS/HSM?
[01:58] Ethan: Yes. For Private and Dedicated we support customer KMS and HSM integrations. For hosted we have KMS integrations, we can also support customer-managed keys for certain enterprise plans. We'll put the exact doc link in the follow-up.
[02:12] Maya: I'll add that to next steps — share our KMS/HSM integration doc + SOC2 pack.
[02:18] Jordan: Great. On the staging side, what do you need from us? IP ranges, service accounts?
[02:24] Ethan: For a staging redwood environment we ask for: one environment table — staging vpc peering or private link details, firewall egress rules, the IP allowlist, and a service account or token to test. If you're trying hosted we only need an onboarding email and user SAML if you want SSO.
[02:40] Priya: I'll capture that. We also need the runbook walkthrough — who will run incident ops if the latency spikes?
[02:46] Maya: We'll assign roles in the runbook. Typically Redwood CSM handles onboarding ops and the SE will hand over runbook to your oncall. In pilot, Redwood SE stays on slack for quick triage.
[02:56] Jordan: Ok fine. Let's quickly sketch the pilot success criteria.
[02:59] Ethan: Possible pilot scope: 2-week staging run, 5k daily concurrent inference tokens (or x qps), latency 95th < 300ms for single-turn generative flows — we can tune batching and caching to get there. Also cost per 1k tokens target, we can model that in the spreadsheet.
[03:18] Jordan: That 300ms number — is that realistic on Hosted?
[03:21] Ethan: It depends on the model and sequence length. For smaller prompt-response pairs on optimized kernels we often see sub-200ms p95 on Dedicated; on hosted you can get close but it varies by load and region. We'll include typical benchmarks.
[03:36] Maya: We'll also provide a benchmark sheet — we'll propose a simple synthetic test and also recommend 10 real prompts for quality checks.
[03:45] Samir: About logs, do you keep raw request bodies? We need to know redaction options and retention policy.
[03:51] Ethan: We can toggle request logging and we have auto-redaction controls for PII in transit. For full compliance you can opt to not store request bodies and only keep hashed artifacts. We'll add the exact toggles to the runbook.
[04:06] Priya: Can you run through the runbook items now?
[04:09] Ethan: Sure, I'll share screen — (pause) alright, runbook section one: Access provisioning. Step A: Create staging project and send admin contact. Step B: Provide IP allowlist, service account or SAML group for the Redwood staging user. Step C: We create staging keys and share them in the secure channel. Step D: Validate sample inference call.
[04:34] Jordan: How long does provisioning take?
[04:36] Ethan: If you give us IPs and a service account, typically 24–48 hours. If you want VPC peering it's 3–5 business days because of your infra tickets.
[04:45] Maya: Noted. Next runbook item: Observability — we'll add steps to configure exporters to push latency traces and token breakdowns into your tracing backend. We recommend instrumenting around the route level.
[04:58] Priya: For tracing, we use OpenTelemetry and Datadog. Any special hooks?
[05:02] Ethan: We have trace hooks and can emit span IDs in response metadata. For Datadog we recommend our APM integration; for OpenTelemetry we provide a collector config.
[05:12] Samir: Do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM?
[05:15] Maya: Yes, S A M L 2.0, and we support SCIM provisioning. We'll need your IdP metadata.
[05:21] Jordan: On the topic of data residency — if we run hosted from US-east but need EU data locality later, how hard is migration?
[05:28] Ethan: It's doable but you should plan for model caching and cold starts; we can route EU traffic to EU region and replicate model pins. It's a deployment migration, not trivial but straightforward with our rollout tools. We'll note caveats in the runbook.
[05:42] Priya: Can we do a short technical deep dive during the pilot about batching and KV cache behavior?
[05:47] Ethan: Absolutely — SE-led session. We'll show how continuous batching affects latency and how to configure prefix/KV cache for your chat flows. Note: sometimes the transcript spells KV cache as K V cash or K V cache — but it's K-V cache.
[05:59] Jordan: Good. What are the SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:03] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets under the reserved capacity contract. Hosted has best-effort with published performance profiles but not the same SLA guarantees. We'll share the SLA doc.
[06:15] Samir: On audit logs, do you provide immutable export to our S3/GCS?
[06:20] Ethan: Yes we support log exports to cloud storage and can integrate with your SIEM. For higher compliance we can configure tamper-evident logs.
[06:30] Priya: Ok let's go over the tentative timeline.
[06:33] Maya: Step 0: Today — activation handshake and runbook assignment. Step 1: Provisioning & keys (target 48 hours). Step 2: Quick smoke tests (2–3 days). Step 3: 2-week staging pilot (tentative window 2026-12-20 to 2027-01-03). Step 4: Review + decide Dedicated vs Private.
[06:55] Jordan: The 2-week window is fine, we'll confirm internal approvals.
[06:58] Samir: I'll need the SOC2 and the dataflow diagrams for our audit team before provisioning.
[07:03] Maya: I'll attach the SOC2 pack and the network/dataflow template.
[07:07] Ethan: Also I'll attach a sample perf script and a small synthetic traffic generator you can run from your staging nodes. It measures p95 and token throughput and dumps a trace for the Redwood tracing link.
[07:19] Priya: Great. A couple of small questions: pricing during pilot — any credits?
[07:24] Maya: We'll apply onboarding credits for the initial pilot; I'll include the breakdown in the email. After pilot we'll share cost modeling based on measured token consumption.
[07:33] Jordan: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[07:36] Ethan: Two common items: JWT token expiration mistakes and unexpected egress rules blocking the KV cache upload. Also keep an eye on request size limits; we can increase them but it needs config.
[07:49] Samir: For keys — can we rotate keys without downtime?
[07:52] Ethan: Yes, key rotation is supported with a small overlap window; we'll detail the steps.
[07:59] Maya: Ok let's recap action items and owners.
[08:02] Maya: Action 1: Maya to send runbook draft, SOC2 pack, KMS doc, and provisional pricing (due 2026-12-13).
[08:12] Ethan: Action 2: Ethan to send perf scripts, sample traces, and a staging checklist (due 2026-12-17).
[08:19] Samir: Action 3: Samir to provide networking ranges, IdP metadata for SAML, and KMS contact (due 2026-12-15).
[08:28] Priya: Action 4: Priya to open infra ticket for VPC peering (if we choose peering) — target 2026-12-11.
[08:36] Jordan: We'll confirm pilot approval internally and reply by EOD Friday.
[08:40] Maya: Great — any final Qs?
[08:42] Jordan: No, thanks. This was helpful.
[08:45] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[08:47] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and links.
[08:50] Maya: Thanks all. Meeting end.
